answer: Use the ocm-channel facility, which lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s). Syntax: show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> [opm-pwr] [connected]. The instance key is name (String, length 0..64) plus lower-frequency and upper-frequency, both uint32, which bound the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point). opm-pwr is the Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 in range -99.00..99.00, default -99. connected yields true if the channel is configured, that is, involved in an oxcon; values true or false, default false. ocm-channel is show-only, available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. On ocm-mp the ocm-enable attribute, which enables regular power monitoring, takes values disabled or enabled and defaults to enabled. Change it with set ocm-mp-<name> ocm-enable <value>; the only other settable attributes are label (String 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Read-only companions: monitoring-state, which the system reports as enabled when an OMS reference exists (default enabled); monitored-port, the port actually being monitored, which can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM (default not-applicable); and ad-direction, the reference to the AD coupler/splitter DWDM port, value ingress. managed-by defaults to system. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

The ocm-ptp facility provides dedicated OCM monitoring and is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG. It is not on out of the box: ocm-enable (enabled or disabled) defaults to disabled, so enable it explicitly, for example set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled. Other settables are label and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Read-only: monitoring-state, default disabled, reported enabled only when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible; ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress); last-measurement, the last OCM scan date and time, default never; and adg-number, uint8 in range 0..110, default 0.

On the oms facility grid-mode defaults to flexible, which allows creating and deleting MCs of different widths. The fixed alternatives are fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100 (50 GHz with 88 C-band channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100) and fixed-150G-40ch. The default spectrum is standard C-band: lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 (191.3 to 196.15 THz). monitoring-mode selects how the OMS is monitored: not-monitored (non-intrusive, no OCM/DGE), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM), dge-fixed-attenuation, ila-with-equalization (with DGE and OCM) and integrated-equalization. Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for ILA, and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes. It is only exposed for an OMS of a port belonging to a degree, or on node-type ILA.

The ops (Optical Physical Section) facility takes: set ops-<name> [label] [admin-state] [alarm-report-control] [input-psd-profile] [role] [port-expansion]. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role defaults to general-purpose and may be tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only on specific RD ports in SLTE l0-mode-op) or active-multi-carrier. port-expansion is no (default) or y-cable, intended for Y-cable expansion. admin-state is lock, unlock or maintenance, default unlock; alarm-report-control is allowed (default) or inhibited. supported-roles is read-only and shows which roles the card, and sometimes card-mode, actually permits. Example: set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency, type Frequency with overall range 0 or 191275000..196125000 MHz, default 0 (zero means not configured); the usable sub-range and step depend on the module and pluggable, for example CHM7 and CHM7X 190625000 to 196725000 MHz in 50 MHz steps, CHM6 191333000 to 196117000 MHz, CHM2TX 191292500 to 196137500 MHz in 1 MHz steps. Yes, you can trim it: frequency-offset is int16 in range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0, used for bright tuning; once set the frequency changes slowly over 1 to 10 s without affecting service. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, Number in range -55.0..55.00 dBm with accuracy adjustable in 0.5 dBm steps, the real range being pluggable-dependent, for example CHM2TX -6 to 0 (default 0) and CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0 (default -2).

Yes, with optical-carrier propagate-shutdown. When it is set, the transmit laser is shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure; the function is mainly used at a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled. Pair it with propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer, the hold off time of propagate shutdown, a Number in range 0..2000 milliseconds, default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card. Set both with set optical-carrier-<name> propagate-shutdown enabled propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer <ms>.

Very little: the optical-channel facility only supports set optical-channel-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>]. label is a user defined String of length 0..256; admin-state is lock, unlock or maintenance with default unlock, for example set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock. Everything else is show-only: name (String 0..64), supporting-card and supporting-port (leafrefs to equipment/card and equipment/card/port), supporting-facilities and supported-facilities (instance identifiers to parent and child facilities), AID (String 1..64), oper-state (enabled or disabled, default disabled), avail-state, and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Read the laser with show optical-ptp-<name> laser-state. It is show-only, values disabled or enabled, default disabled, and reports the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state; for RD amplifiers it means the source (Tx) pump, and it is only of relevance for DWDM line ports. Yes, you can add fixed pad on receive: fix-rx-attenuation is the fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB means no fixed attenuator. Example: set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10. The Tx counterpart fix-tx-attenuation has the same 0..30 dB range and default 0 but is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Measured powers are power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx, -99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99 dBm.

On optical-switch the Signal Fail decision uses working-los-threshold and protection-los-threshold, which define the SF threshold for the Working and Protection paths in dBm. Both are settable, range -55.0 to 0 dBm, default -23 dBm. Signal Degrade uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold, same -55.0 to 0 dBm range, default -18 dBm, and SD-based switching only happens when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). facility-los-threshold sets the facility port threshold below which loss of signal is declared, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Hysteresis: los-threshold-hysteresis (SF) defaults to 3 dB and switch-threshold-hysteresis (SD) to 2 dB, each 0.5 to 5.0 dB in 0.1 dB steps, with 1 dB recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

set osc-<name> accepts label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, l0-comm-interface-type, osc-control, target-output-power, tx-power-adjustment, voa-attenuation-target-rx and lof-soak-timer. osc-control is auto (default) or manual; auto has been supported since R6.0.1, and HSC OLS nodes support auto only. target-output-power is the OSC Tx power at the DWDM line port output, na (default) or -2.5..4.5 dBm. tx-power-adjustment trims the automatically calculated Tx target, na or -6..6 dB, default 0. voa-attenuation-target-rx is the Rx VOA target for manual mode, 0..30 dB, default 10. l0-comm-interface-type is ipv4 or ipv6; ipv4 for standard OLS, ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS. lof-soak-timer is short (default, about 3 ms) or long (adds 18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms) and is only visible on the PBAx card. Read-only: osc-mode, osc-wavelength, voa-attenuation-actual-rx, power-actual-rx/tx.

Use show otdr-<name> otdr-state. It indicates the current status of the OTDR and a status change triggers a change notification. Values: not-available (default, status not available), idle, measuring (measurement ongoing), finished (measurement completed) and fail (measurement failed). When it fails, otdr-error carries the error message produced when the measurement ends with error. While running, otdr-measurement-time shows the time remaining in the current measurement (integer, default 0), otdr-measurement-port shows the OTDR port under test with 0 meaning the card is not measuring any port, otdr-measurement-direction shows not-available, tx or rx, and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile shows none, short, medium, long or raman-precheck1/2/3. otdr-laser-state reports not-available, enabled or disabled.

On otdr-ptp: otdr-range sets the distance range in km used to calculate the measurement repetition period, auto (default) or 0...300.0 km, and should be the actual fibre length plus 10 percent; from R9.1, if the OTS can be traced from the fiber connection between the ILA/ROADM card and OTDR8OFP2, it is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/fiber-length-rx with 10 percent margin rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-pulse-width is auto or 10...20,000 ns. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or 0.4...100.0. otdr-measurement-speed is auto (default), fast (about 10 s), medium (about 15 s), slow (about 1 minute), precision (3 to 5 minutes) or high-precision (5 to 7 minutes). otdr-ior is auto or 1.0...2.0, peak-power auto or 5...14.5, and launching-fiber-length 0...50 m, default 0, with auto not supported.

On the ots facility. Declare fibre with fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx, both defaulting to SSMF, chosen from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor (rx also allows not-applicable, auto and not-configured). Length is fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx, auto (default) or 0..500.0 km, required for tilt control and for Raman backward pumping. Loss is span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 0..80 dB (receive also accepts 99, meaning not configured), default 0; changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. Extra pad goes in external-attenuation-tx and external-attenuation-rx, 0..30 dB, default 0. span-loss-reference selects configured or measured (default measured), and span-loss-aging-margin-rx is 0.00..10.00 dB, default 1.0.

The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated by the system on line card provisioning; you never create it. The format is ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>, so an RD20TM DWDM line gives show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line, and a C2ILASGH with two lines gives ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2. Only two attributes are settable: nmoper-alarm-reporting (disabled by default; when enabled a mismatch between expected-operator and rx-operator raises the NMOPER alarm, and disabling it clears the alarm immediately and stops the comparison) and expected-operator (up to 32 characters). tx-operator is defaulted by the system to <ne-name>-D00, and rx-operator, tti-style (ITU-T-G709 by default) and tti-port-id are show-only.

ots-r assumes SSMF: required-fiber-type-rx, the required fibre type on the DWDM Line with reference to the Rx fibre, defaults to SSMF and accepts AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor. It is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and there is no fiber-connection. You can also declare fiber-length-rx (unspecified by default, or 0..500.0), span-loss-receive (default 99), external-attenuation-rx, and delta-pointloss, the additional Rx attenuation determined after turning up pumps, not-applicable (default) or -1..3.5 dB. target-power-setting is manual or auto, default auto. Show-only: configured-fiber-type-rx, configured-fiber-length-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx and connected-reference.

Yes, and it does depend on that. The ots-r-auto-otdr attribute automatic-otdr enables or disables OTDR based automatic fiber check; its default is enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. It also defaults to enabled if the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with an integrated OTDR, and is disabled if the NE has a Raman card that is not aggregated with the EDFA card. The setting persists over warm and cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling while a test is running aborts it and releases the amplifier that the automatic OTDR had blocked; if none is running, no further tests are triggered until re-enabled. Progress shows in auto-otdr-state: not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail or aborted. loss-calibration-by-otdr is none (green field), rx-only, tx-only or tx-rx.

Create it with add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [label] [activation-mode] [auto-delete] [activation-request-fwd] [activation-request-bwd] [direction] [target-output-power-src] [target-output-power-dst] [circuit-id], for example add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'. direction is two-way (default) or one-way. Whether it comes up on its own depends on activation-mode: automatic means the service is activated automatically by the system on creation and deactivated on deletion, and it is the default in the standard L0 mode of operation. In SLTE mode the default is manual and in HSC OLS mode activate-on-create, both controlled through activation-request-fwd/bwd (no-request, activate, deactivate). target-output-power-src and -dst are -18.00..15.00 dBm.

Only on RD20TM, and only when it is operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul; profile-control applies to no other card. Syntax: profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>], access Operational Mode only. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power. direction is tx or rx, but for power-profile only tx is supported. For card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. Attenuation profile-data is <StartFreq>,<SlotWidth>,<AttnValue1>,...: for OMS values are 0 to 25.50 dB and N is 776 for standard C-band at 6.25 GHz; for NMC values are -10 to 25.50 and N cannot exceed 32.

Almost nothing optical. set pump-<name> only accepts label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance) and alarm-report-control (allowed, default, or inhibited). Every other pump attribute is show-only: name, supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled or disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user, where only user-created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. To change pump power you need the separate pump-power command, set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>. Access for pump is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>, where pump-id is the integer number of the pump. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power in dBm and applies when control-mode is manual; the range is -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable (the default), with 0 used for the not-applicable case. On an RPBM card the value must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value falls outside the operating range of the Raman sled the alarm PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) is raised. Read the allowed limits with show pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> min-target-pump-power max-target-pump-power, each decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows what is programmed in hardware, derived automatically if control-mode is auto, and actual-pump-power shows the measured value, default -99.

Use show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state, for example show raman-calibration-1-8. It reports the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process: not-available (default, calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration has occurred), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale because of OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss and similar) and fail (ended with a failure). last-calibration-timestamp gives when the last calibration rpc completed, with or without errors, as date-and-time or never (default never). When the state is fail or out-dated, additional-info (string, 0..1024) carries troubleshooting information. Also available: intermediate-results, gain-calibration-error (residual gain error per iteration, in dB) and calibrated-delta-pointloss (-3..3.5 dB).

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. It reports the pilot tone power in both directions: rsc-power-rx is the received Pilot Tone integrated power and rsc-power-tx is the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power, both show-only. Syntax: set rsc-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>], and show rsc-<name> adds supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, label, admin-state, oper-state, avail-state, managed-by, alarm-report-control, rsc-power-rx and rsc-power-tx. admin-state is Unlock, Locked, Maintenance or Unknown, default Unlocked; oper-state is enabled or disabled, default enabled; alarm-report control is Allowed (default) or Inhibited; managed-by defaults to system. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the OMS beneath it is not in a monitoring mode that creates one. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer, OMS, has monitoring-mode configured either as non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the existence of the managed object depends entirely on the OMS monitoring-mode. The object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE. Set the OMS monitoring-mode accordingly and the spectrum object appears. Once present it exposes attenuation-setting, a unique attenuation value for the entire spectrum in the range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable only when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw, plus the read-only dge-in-use, which reports true when the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization.

Use spectrum-control, whose key is name plus direction plus center-frequency: set spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [attenuation-target <value>] [target-output-power <value>], for example set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1. direction is ingress or egress, but currently only egress is supported and it is the default. center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for the spectra, range 0..30 dB, default 0, and is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer or equivalent is in use (dge-in-use = true). target-output-power is not-specified (default) or -55..55 dBm. show adds width (detected width in MHz, 0 if no match or no DGE fibre-connected) and attenuation-actual.
